content:
A survey of thousands of 9to5Mac readers shows that Apple price hikes are likely to slow down the upgrade cycle, even among the most enthusiastic customer base.

Reducing upgrade frequency was the most common response from readers, far surpassing other options; only 9% of respondents said price increases would not affect their purchasing behavior……

As we have noted before, some increases exceed 50%, and memory and storage upgrades have even doubled on some models — all signs suggest the situation will not improve in the short term.

If you were to guess which group of people would most likely grit their teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same frequency, you might assume it would be 9to5Mac readers, but a survey on Friday shows that even this group has its limits.

Over 90% of readers said they would change their purchasing behavior due to price hikes, with more than one-third saying they would upgrade less frequently.

  • Reduce upgrade frequency: 38%
  • Wait for price drops: 14%
  • Give up one or more Apple products: 12%
  • Buy a lower-tier model: 9%
  • No impact: 9%

Reader comments:

Of course, new features could still change people's minds, but at the very least, this result gives reason to expect Apple to notice slowing sales and potentially offer some level of price cuts to maintain demand.
